039.alt: The handwritten sign. The yellow legal pad carries the moment's two-word message. Its ordinary paper and improvised lettering are central to the real stunt, bringing a personal appeal into a televised policy hearing.
The no signs plaque. This invented wall fixture makes the raised sign a visual joke about the room's rules. It is illustrative staging, not a claim that this plaque hung at the hearing.

The report heading. MONETARY POLICY REPORT identifies the business of Yellen's appearance. The drawn document is a contextual prop, not a facsimile of her papers or evidence that she wrote the annotations.

The rounded price note. BTC approximately $2,400 evokes a reported price that afternoon. The amount is rounded for the illustration and does not establish Bitcoin's price at the instant the sign appeared.
The 16 btc flashforward. This small annotation points to the original sign's 2024 winning auction bid. It deliberately reaches forward seven years; it is not a note made at the 2017 hearing.

040.alt: THE BNB FOLDER. BNB / ICO 2017 connects the new exchange to the preceding token sale. The folder is an illustrative prop, not an authenticated company document.
THE JULY CALENDAR. July 2017 anchors the launch month. The card date, 14 July, is supported by Zhao’s retrospective; the calendar is invented staging.
BUY BITCOIN. The yellow note is a deliberate callback to card 039 and its handwritten sign. It is not claimed to have appeared in the real office.

THE MODEST RECEPTION. The glass doorway, counter, wall sign and plants draw on office-tour footage. This environmental detail recalls the startup’s small beginnings; the footage’s exact recording date and address are unverified.

041.alt: THE SHARED BLOCK. 478,558 is the last common block. The plaque marks the shared history before the two chains diverged; it is not the number of Bitcoin Cash’s first distinct block.
THE 8 MB PLAQUE. This refers to Bitcoin Cash’s initial block-size limit in August 2017, not its present limit, a transaction count or a guarantee of speed.
THE MATCHING LEDGERS. Identical books symbolise the common transaction record inherited by both networks. No real historical books or physical coin duplication are claimed.

THE CAPACITY PLANS. Both drawings show a linear sequence of blocks. Larger boxes and more slips on the BCH plan illustrate extra capacity. They are not to scale or literal software diagrams, and do not imply a different block interval.

042.alt: THE 481,824 PLAQUE. The stone plaque marks the Bitcoin block where SegWit became active on 24 August 2017. It anchors the transformation to a specific point in the chain.

THE BIP 141 PLATE. The larger bull's armour names the Bitcoin Improvement Proposal defining SegWit's consensus rules, including its witness commitment and block-weight limit. It is a technical reference, not a manufacturer's badge.

GOLD AND BLUE CHANNELS. Gold transaction tiles and blue witness channels make the data separation visible. Both belong to the same Bitcoin transaction and blockchain. The colours are an artistic key, not a literal protocol diagram.

THE LIGHTNING FORESHADOW. The bolt and storm point toward Lightning payment channels. They foreshadow later development; Lightning Labs announced its first lnd mainnet beta in March 2018, after SegWit's activation.

043.alt: THE DATED NOTICE. The clipboard reads 04 SEP 2017, the date of the joint announcement. Its delivery turns a busy token market into a moment of interruption. The prop is an illustration, not a reproduction of an official form.

THE REFUND TRAY. The tray marked REFUNDS references the instruction for completed token offerings to make clearance and refund arrangements. Its envelopes are imagined props, not evidence from a particular project.

THE UNFINISHED PITCH. An upward chart is left on the sales board as the discussion stops. It symbolises fundraising interrupted, without accusing a named project of fraud or promising that prices would keep rising.

THE PACKED POWER CABLE. The small coil on the equipment case points forward to China's 2021 mining crackdown and card 072. It is an intentional collection crossover, not a mining restriction in the September 2017 ICO notice.

044.alt: SOFIA TO ATHENS. The itinerary names the route recorded by the FBI for 25 October 2017. It anchors the disappearance to a documented journey. The ticket is an invented prop, not a reproduction of her travel document.
THE DATE TAG. 25 OCT 2017 marks the selected moment. Its placement beside the folder links the theatrical scene to the historical date, without suggesting that this tag existed.
THE UNTAKEN MICROPHONE. The empty speaking position recalls OneCoin's public promotional spectacle. The theatre and curtain exit are symbolic staging, not evidence of an actual farewell performance.

THE FOLDER AND CONFETTI. The OneCoin folder represents the sales pitch left behind. Scattered confetti points forward to card 045, BitConnect, as a collection crossover about promotional spectacle. It does not imply a relationship between the organisations.

045.alt: THE MINIATURE CAR. The small sports car recalls luxury-car awards to leading promoters at the convention. Its placement is symbolic; it does not claim that Matos won a car or that this model stood onstage.
25,610. The number on the plinth is the US-dollar amount Matos later said he invested. It is a self-reported investment, not an audited balance, a prize value or a promised return.
THE CRACKED PYRAMID. The broken gold pyramid is a retrospective metaphor for the scheme's failure. It brings knowledge of the later collapse into the illustration; it is not a documented stage prop.

THE INVESTOR LANYARD. The badge makes Matos's role explicit: investor and viral speaker. It is an illustrative label, not a reproduction of an authenticated event badge. BitConnect's founder was Satish Kumbhani.

046.alt: THE PARENT TRAIT CARDS. PARENT A and PARENT B point towards a new kitten. They explain the game's trait-combination mechanic through an illustrated workshop diagram. The cards are invented props, and the breeding is a software process.

THE PENDING TAGS. The stacked tags turn delayed transactions into a visible backlog. They refer to congestion in early December, after the 28 November launch. They do not represent lost kittens or documented delivery slips.
THE IMPATIENT PAW. The raised paw and pink hourglass make waiting personal. This is a comic expression of the player's experience, not a recorded incident or a timer for the release of new cats.

THE STILL-LIT ETHEREUM BOX. The illuminated box recalls Ethereum's first-light motif elsewhere in the collection. Its continuing glow links the game to the network beneath it: busy and under strain. The electrical box is a symbolic crossover, not historical equipment.

047.alt: THE PETH VESSEL. The violet vessel names Pooled Ether, the collateral used by the original system. Its larger volume suggests overcollateralisation, without claiming that the artwork measures a fixed collateral ratio.

THE CDP LOCK. The padlock marked CDP stands for a Collateralized Debt Position. It points to collateral locked while Dai debt is outstanding. The valve and padlock are invented visual shorthand for smart contracts.
THE ONE-DOLLAR TARGET. The central dial explicitly says TARGET $1. It represents Dai's soft peg, not a promise that its market price could never move away from one dollar.

THE MAINTENANCE WRENCH. The wrench at the lower right suggests ongoing risk management and parameter decisions. It is an artistic prop, not documented equipment. See the full illustration for this detail beneath the card's title area.

048.alt: THE BETA PLAQUE. The chest plaque reads lnd 0.4-beta. It identifies the specific software release, anchoring the scene to Lightning Labs' first mainnet beta rather than the invention of Lightning itself.
THE HANGING DATE. The tag reads 15 MAR 2018, the release announcement's date. It records this milestone, not the date of the first Lightning idea or the first payment ever made.

THE BITCOIN CLASPS. Two Bitcoin clasp halves are joined by light. They suggest the two participants in a funded channel, whose balances can change off-chain while their channel remains anchored to Bitcoin's blockchain.

THE SPHINX BRACER. The engraved Sphinx nods to the Sphinx-derived packet format used for Lightning onion routing. Layered instructions guide a payment through its route. The mythical engraving is an artistic clue, not actual networking equipment.

049.alt: THE PAIRED RESERVES. ETH and ERC20 label the two chambers. Together they represent one V1 exchange's paired reserves. Pouring into both suggests providing liquidity; a swap instead adds one asset and removes some of the other.

THE CONSTANT-PRODUCT PLATE. The x*y=k engraving recalls the pricing rule. The reserve ratio changes as trades occur. Fees and liquidity changes affect the reserve product, so the inscription does not promise a fixed price or an unchanging k.

THE V1 BADGE. V1 identifies the original protocol generation. Its exchanges paired a token with ETH, and token-to-token swaps could route through ETH. The badge keeps the scene distinct from later Uniswap versions.
THE LAUNCH DATE. 2 NOV 2018 marks the public launch on Ethereum mainnet during Devcon 4 in Prague. It is visible on the engine in the full artwork and repeated at the top of the framed card.

050.alt: THE PINE PLAQUE. The pineapple and PINE name point to the fund's pseudonymous founder. This invented plaque is a storytelling clue, not a documented dedication at a particular water point.
THE WATER TEST KIT. Sample vials and a colour comparison strip represent continuing water-quality checks. The gift supported testing and maintenance as well as new infrastructure.

THE BITCOIN CASE. The Bitcoin symbol connects the technician's everyday tools to a cryptocurrency-funded gift. It links an abstract asset to practical work without identifying Pine or a real field team.

THE IMPACT NOTEBOOK. 37 PROJECTS recalls The Water Project's impact account. The 2019 notation signals the later reporting context; it does not date all 37 completions to 2018 or identify this fictional scene as a documented visit.

052.alt: THE BALANCE SHEETS. The oversized client ledger and small asset sheet visualise the imbalance. Their torn edges are symbolic; they do not depict actual destroyed records or establish how evidence was handled.
C$215M OWED. The bundle names the approximate Canadian-dollar value owed to clients in the OSC reconstruction. It represents liabilities, not a pile of cash or the amount locked inside the safe.

THE CLAIMS BOX. The files stand for affected clients seeking recovery. They are invented props, not copies of actual claim forms. The figure holding a folder is a fictional adult, not an identified claimant.

THE HIDDEN KEY NOTE. A printed key note is tucked among folders below the balances sheet. It recalls the access narrative as a secondary clue, not a discovered usable key. OSC staff attributed most losses to misconduct.

051.alt: THE DATE TAG. The satchel's tag reads 19 JAN 2019, marking the experiment's start. It dates the historical event, not a documented meeting in this harbour.
THE STARTING RECEIPT. The slip tucked into the satchel records the initial 100,000-satoshi payment. It is an invented prop representing that amount, not an original receipt.
THE TRAVEL SATCHEL. A globe motif, travel stamps and Bitcoin pin suggest the relay's international reach and currency. They do not identify particular stops or a physical route.
THE LANTERN INCREMENT. The lantern's +10,000 SATS mark recalls the requested addition before each onward payment. The lantern symbolises the torch; actual contributions were not always uniform.

053.alt: THE DATE PLAQUE. The first beacon carries 30 MAY 2019, the launch-announcement date.
THE PRICE SCREEN. Its ETH/USD screen identifies the initial reference feed. The rising line is an illustrative graphic, not a historical price chart.

THE THREE BEACONS. I, II and III recall three data sources and three independent node operators. Their blue beams connect directly to the city; they simplify the system rather than diagram its exact architecture.

THE ETHEREUM CITY. An oversized Ethereum symbol rises above the finished city. The back-facing traveller offers a viewpoint into this imagined on-chain world, without representing a documented person.

054.alt: THE BLUE GLOBE. An oversized illuminated Earth gives physical form to Libra’s worldwide ambition. Its scale is symbolic; the display is an invented presentation device.
THE LIBRA EMBLEM. Three wave-like lines and the Libra name identify the proposed project on the plinth. The emblem anchors the scene to the 2019 announcement.
THE PROJECT PAPER. The observer holds a document marked Project Libra. It represents a proposal under consideration, rather than an operational currency or a facsimile of a historical document.
THE OBSERVERS. The thoughtful figures suggest questions about trust and governance. Blue light connects them to the globe; their identities and this meeting are fictional.

055.alt: THE RETURNING HODLER. The black hoodie, Bitcoin mug and network poster echo card 021. This is the collection’s fictional character, not a portrait of a documented investor.
12 MAR 2020. The fallen calendar anchors Black Thursday. Towering red candlesticks and the wrecked city turn pandemic fear and market losses into visual metaphor.
MAKER AUCTION / 0 DAI. The newspaper refers to some MakerDAO collateral auctions that cleared for zero DAI. It is external news, not a receipt showing the character’s Bitcoin being liquidated.
THE BEAR MARKET. The giant bear towers over the fallen HODL character, turning a market sell-off into a physical threat. Its weight amid the rubble makes the pressure of the crash visible.

056.alt: MAINNET BETA / 16 MAR 2020. The foreground plaque anchors the scene to Solana's launch date. Beta signals an initial live network whose capabilities were still being expanded.
THE PoH EQUIPMENT. The small PoH labels point to Proof of History, Solana's verifiable clock. The separate VALIDATORS equipment recalls the people and machines maintaining consensus.
RAYDIUM / COMING 2021. The left-hand stall looks ahead to Raydium's 2021 launch. Its bright sign is a hindsight clue, not a documented 2020 announcement.
JUPITER / COMING 2021. The planet-shaped sign points to Jupiter's 2021 arrival as a swap aggregator. This future attraction is deliberately placed here with hindsight.
BONK / COMING 2022. The dog mascot foreshadows BONK, launched on Christmas Day 2022. It belongs to the scene's retrospective future, not the mainnet-beta launch.
PUMP.FUN / COMING 2024. The right-hand balloon stall refers to Pump.fun's January 2024 launch. Its later date makes the artwork's forward-looking, hindsight construction explicit.

057.alt: PROPOSAL 007. The plaque on the sluice points to the governance proposal that enabled user distribution on 15 June 2020. The gate marks that change, not the creation of lending itself.
0.50 COMP / BLOCK. The seed-machine plate records the initial release per Ethereum block, estimated then at 2,880 COMP daily. It describes token distribution, not an interest rate or promised yield.

SUPPLY 50% / BORROW 50%. The trays split one market's allocation between its suppliers and borrowers. Each user's share still depended on their balance; the picture does not promise equal amounts per person.

COMP SEEDS AND BALLOT BOX. The packet and voting slip connect participation to governance. COMP holders could delegate voting authority. The seeds are distinct from the water, keeping governance rewards separate from lending liquidity.

059.alt: 21,454 BTC / $250m. The plate records the announced purchase. The $250 million total includes fees and expenses; the gold stacks are a visual metaphor, not a literal inventory of physical bitcoins.
THE TREASURY FOLDER. TREASURY RESERVE and 11 AUG 2020 tie the folder to the policy announcement. This fictional prop anchors the scene to a dated corporate decision.
THE CASH TRAY. Notes remain in the lower drawer, keeping cash visible beside the new reserve asset. The image avoids an all-cash-converted claim; it does not quantify a remaining cash balance.
THE FUTURE CAR. The envelope marked FUTURE foreshadows Tesla's February 2021 disclosure. It is an intentional later reference, not evidence of a meeting, shared plan or historical envelope.

060.alt: THE UNICORN JAR. The unicorn refers to Uniswap and calls back to card 049. The jar is a fictional shorthand for pooled liquidity, not evidence of a stolen reserve or a real container.

LP SHARES. The receipt represents liquidity-provider tokens: transferable claims on pool assets. Staking eligible Uniswap LP tokens in MasterChef earned SUSHI and made those deposited claims available for migration.
SUSHI REWARDS. The menu points to the token incentives used to attract providers. It depicts the 2020 liquidity-mining offer; no reward rate, token price or guaranteed return is stated.
THE SMILING FANG. The friendly fang charm names the vampire strategy in miniature. Its smile reinforces the chef's invitation and the providers' voluntary participation in the liquidity migration.

061.alt: THE 400 UNI CARGO. The crate label recalls the fixed grant for each eligible historical user address. It does not describe the separately calculated liquidity-provider allocation or promise a future token price.

THREE PINK PARACHUTES. Bright pink canopies repeat the delivery motif across the cloudscape. The three illustrated drops create scale and rhythm; they are not a count of recipients or categories of eligibility.

THE CARGO AIRCRAFT. The plane makes the word airdrop literal in the picture. The aircraft and sunset cloud sea are imaginative staging for a digital distribution, not a reconstruction of an actual flight.

062.alt: THE ETHEREUM BEACON. The Ethereum-shaped light inside the lantern sends a violet beam over the harbor. The lighthouse visualizes the new consensus chain coming online.
12:00:23 UTC. The plaque above the door records the precise genesis time on 1 December 2020. The seconds distinguish it from the earlier noon minimum-time setting.
THE MINIMUM THRESHOLD. The sign pairs 16,384 with 32 ETH each: 524,288 ETH in minimum qualifying deposits. MINIMUM matters; this is a launch threshold, not an actual genesis-validator count.
FOUR CLIENT PLAQUES. Lighthouse, Nimbus, Prysm and Teku appear beside the doorway. These names identify launch-era client software, rather than four validators or four physical institutions.

THE MINE AND UNFINISHED BRIDGE. Lit mining rigs across the water recall Mainnet continuing under proof-of-work. The missing bridge span signals that uniting the two systems still lay ahead, at The Merge in September 2022.

063.alt: THE JANUARY TAB. JAN 2021 marks the investment-policy change. It does not establish a purchase day. The tab sits above the report, separating that timing from the February receipt.
BITCOIN AND $1.50B. The highlighted pair names the asset and aggregate investment. Their yellow strips form the scene's focal point; the surrounding page lines are illustrative.
NOTE 23 AND THE FILING RECEIPT. NOTE 23 points to Subsequent Events. The separate receipt carries the filing date, 08 FEB 2021. The paper design is invented, not an authentic SEC facsimile.
THE RETURNING PROFESSOR. White hair, goggles and a lab coat bring back the fictional professor from card 047. He acts as the collection's observer, not a real Tesla employee or historical witness.
THE FUTURE ENVELOPE. A car silhouette on the FUTURE envelope echoes card 059. This cross-card clue sits beside the filing, linking the collection's visual stories without making a historical claim.

064.alt: THE FIVE THOUSAND GRID. The 5000 plaque identifies the daily-work theme. The huge colour grid is newly invented imagery, not a copy of the auctioned collage or its individual pictures.
THE AUCTION RESULT. The sheet records ONLINE SALE, $69,346,250 and 11 MAR 2021. These refer to the published sale result. The paper itself is an invented prop, not an original auction document.
THE TOKEN AND MINT DATE. JPG / TOKEN 40913 and MINTED 16 FEB 2021 come from the lot record. The plaque separates the digital object's identifier and mint date from the later sale.
THE DAILY DATES. The catalogue carries 01 MAY 2007 and 07 JAN 2021, the endpoints given in Beeple's archive. Its miniature grid echoes the larger image, tracing the work back to daily practice.

065.alt: THE TWENTY-ONE COUNTDOWN. The giant 21 recalls the ceremony's 21-second digital countdown. Nasdaq identified it as a reference to Bitcoin's maximum supply of 21 million. It is a countdown clue, not a stock price.

THE CLASS A SHARES. COIN / CLASS A identifies Coinbase's ticker and the class of common stock listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. The strip distinguishes shares in the company from the crypto assets on its platform.

THE DIRECT LISTING. DIRECT LISTING names the route Coinbase used to go public. Nasdaq's opening auction was to establish the first public trading price. This label is an explanatory addition to the imagined display.

THE REMOTE CELEBRATION. Four video windows recall a ceremony conducted remotely across the country. These illustrated participants are fictional; neither their identities nor the number and arrangement of windows reproduce an exact broadcast frame.

066.alt: THE TEN THOUSAND TAGS. The 10,000 sign above the hanging tags points to the collection's fixed supply. The small rack is an illustrative shorthand for that total, not a literal inventory or a documented launch-day object.
THE MINT PRICE. MINT 0.08 ETH records the original price to mint an ape. Ethereum transaction gas was an additional cost. The sign refers to the initial mint, not a later resale value.

THE MEMBERSHIP READER. The portrait card and green reader translate NFT membership into a physical doorway. Both props are invented symbols; the illustration does not claim that BAYC used this hardware or issued these plastic cards.

THE PIXEL PORTRAIT POSTCARD. The postcard uses an actual crop of approved HISTROVE 038 artwork, including its small 10,000 caption. Perspective-fitted inside the original paper border, it is a deliberate cross-card reference to CryptoPunks.

067.alt: THE ON AIR SIGN. The illuminated sign marks the threshold of live television. It anchors the scene to the broadcast moment, while the exact sign and backstage view are illustrative inventions.

THE WEEKEND UPDATE DESK. The desk names the segment where Musk played Lloyd Ostertag and discussed Dogecoin. The recognisable setting is an artistic interpretation, not a frame copied from the broadcast.

THE STUDIO CAMERAS. The cameras turn the empty desk into a scene prepared for an audience. Their placement symbolises television's reach; it does not document the actual studio's equipment or floor plan.
DOGE AT THE CURTAIN. The suit and curtain place the meme in a performer's waiting position. Doge is a fictional stand-in for the coin's public moment; no real dog on the SNL set is being depicted.

068.alt: THE BLACK HOLE. The dark centre stands for an inaccessible burn address. It is a visual metaphor for giving up token control, not a claim about physics or a real event in space.
THE DOG-FACED COINS. The Shiba Inu faces identify the SHIB theme. These illustrated coins represent digital tokens; their count and size do not encode the amount burned.
THE SINGLE INWARD TRAIL. The shrinking coin stream has one endpoint inside the dark centre. It symbolises the burn transfer, with no separate charity route shown in this scene.

THE OBSERVER AT THE WINDOW. The figure and straight spacecraft frame place the viewer outside the spectacle. The setting and pose are invented; they do not document Buterin performing the transaction.

069.alt: THE BASE FEE BOWL. The dragon's flame meets the coin above the BASE FEE label. This visualises the protocol burn: the base-fee payment was destroyed rather than collected in a miner's wallet.
THE SEPARATE TIP BOWL. Unburned coins sit in the smaller bowl marked TIP. Priority fees remained payable to miners in August 2021. The illustrated coin counts do not measure a real fee split.
THE FOREHEAD EMBLEM. The Ethereum symbol on the dragon's forehead identifies the network behind the mechanism. The creature is an invented personification of the rule, not a historical actor.
BIG BEN IN THE DISTANCE. The small clock tower names London through a recognisable landmark. It is a clue to the upgrade's title, not evidence that the network change happened at a London toll gate.

070.alt: THE ETHEREUM CHEST. The large chest bears Ethereum's diamond emblem. It points to one of the three affected networks. The gold treasure is a visual shorthand for varied crypto assets, not a measured pile of ETH.

THE BSC POUCH. The left-hand pouch carries the Binance emblem, referencing Binance Smart Chain, the network's name in 2021. This is one part of a cross-chain incident, not a claim that Binance's exchange was hacked.
THE POLYGON POUCH. The right-hand pouch bears Polygon's linked emblem. Together with the chest and BSC pouch, it makes the three-chain reach visible. Poly Network and Polygon are distinct projects.

THE UNEXPECTED HANDOVER. The pirate's gloved hands guide the open chest toward the surprised recipient. The handover symbolises recovery over time. Both people and the ship's cabin are invented; the pirate is neither an identified attacker nor a claim of heroism.

071.alt: TWO WAYS TO PAY. The counter sign pairs dollar and Bitcoin symbols above a rectangular cash box. They express the coexistence of familiar cash and a new digital payment method; the illustrated notes and coins do not specify a price.

THE LAUNCH-DAY CALENDAR. The wall calendar reads 7 SEP 2021. It anchors the artwork to the day Bitcoin's legal-tender status took effect, rather than implying that the whole national transition happened in a single meal.

THE OPEN NOTEBOOK. A pencil rests on a lined notebook in the foreground. It symbolises the merchant's everyday task of keeping accounts. No legible prices or conversion calculation are shown, so those should not be inferred.
THE SALVADORAN FLAG. Blue and white bands place the scene in El Salvador. The street and distant buildings are an imagined setting, not an identified town, landmark or real business.

072.alt: NOTICE 1283. The wall notice pairs 1283 with 2021.09.03. Both point to the national mining directive: 3 September is its signed date, while the card's 24 September date marks publication. The illustrated paperwork is a stylised prop.

MAY AND JUNE. The MAY 2021 and JUN 2021 crate labels anchor the earlier crackdown. May brought the national call against Bitcoin mining and trading; June brought shutdown measures. Packing and relocation were underway before September's published notice.

THE ICO 2017 FILE. The folder marked ICO 2017 recalls China's earlier intervention against token fundraising. That announcement ordered token-financing activities to stop and restricted exchange services. It supplies regulatory background rather than dating this warehouse scene.

THE UNADDRESSED TAG. The right-hand crate carries a blank shipping tag and an upward handling arrow. Together with the packed machine, they suggest equipment in transit and the work of relocation. No destination or departure date is written into this imagined shipment.

073.alt: THE ROOT MARKER. The Bitcoin symbol on the old bronze plaque beside the roots identifies the established tree. It anchors the grafting metaphor: Taproot added spending capabilities to Bitcoin through a soft fork, preserving continuity with the existing chain.

BLOCK 709632. The small horizontal tag hanging beside the graft reads 709632. That number identifies the block height at which Taproot became active on 14 November 2021. It marks activation itself, after the earlier miner signalling process.

THE SCHNORR TOOLS. The open tool roll carries the SCHNORR label beneath its brown-handled tools. It links practical craft to the signature scheme specified by BIP 340, one component of the upgrade alongside Taproot's construction and Tapscript's rules.

THE SEGWIT CHARM. The small train charm at the gardener's waist has two connected compartments. This invented keepsake recalls SegWit, the earlier upgrade whose witness framework Taproot builds upon. Taproot outputs use SegWit version 1, continuing that technical lineage.

074.alt: THE PEOPLE PADDLE. The foreground paddle reads PEOPLE, matching ConstitutionDAO's contribution token. Lowered in the bidder's hand, this invented prop stands for the many individual contributors behind the attempt. It is not an authentic paddle used at Sotheby's.

THE SOLD SCREEN. The large illuminated SOLD screen announces that the auction is over. It points to the moment ConstitutionDAO lost the contest, rather than a purchase by the community. The screen's placement and appearance are artistic inventions.

THE 1787 PLAQUE. The small brass plaque beneath the document reads 1787. It identifies the year of the Constitution's first printing and also echoes Sotheby's lot number for this sale. The plaque itself belongs to the imagined display.

THE PRINTED CONSTITUTION. The tall framed paper sheet recalls the first printing of the Constitution's final text. Its dense single-column layout distinguishes the printed document being auctioned from the familiar handwritten original. The illustration is not a facsimile.

075.alt: THE THREE CREATURES. The green, orange and blue creatures recall a team of three Axies. Their glowing, pixelated edges bring digital assets into the player's room as an artistic metaphor. They are not physical pets or real holograms.

THE LOANED ROSTER. The wall sheet reads LOANED TEAM above three creature portraits. It makes the scholarship arrangement visible: the player has access to someone else's Axies. This invented roster represents borrowed assets, rather than proof of ownership.

THE SHARED REWARDS. The notebook separates PLAYER and OWNER into two columns, recalling how scholarship rewards were shared. Its simple marks record no amounts or percentages. The illustrated split describes this arrangement without assigning every scholarship identical terms.

THE MOBILE SESSION. The player holds a phone sideways with both hands, its screen facing her. Axie's early application supported mobile play. Here the gesture emphasises attention and participation; no visible game interface, balance or earnings are claimed.

076.alt: THE DIGITAL QR. The television code recalls the advert's invitation to scan. This artwork uses HISTROVE's public digital destination, /scan/076/, rather than Coinbase's original signup page. It is an interpretive replacement, not a reproduction of the historical code.

THE BLACK SCREEN. The broad black space around the code recalls the original commercial's stripped-back presentation. Its emptiness interrupts the warm, detailed room. The still image suggests the moving advert without inventing a visible trail or additional message.

THE OPPOSING COLOURS. Blue and gold on the left recall Rams supporters; black and orange on the right recall Bengals supporters. The fictional fans share one screen. These emblem-free shirts suggest team loyalties, not exact Super Bowl uniforms.

THE FOOTBALL CASE. A football rests in a clear display case beneath the television. Together with the framed sports pictures, it establishes the fictional bar's atmosphere. It is an invented prop, with no claimed signature or match provenance.

077.alt: THE DONATION TERMINAL. Bitcoin and Ethereum symbols reference two officially listed donation channels. The screen and workstation are illustrative.
THE DATED REPORT. 03 MAR 2022 and $53M+ mark the reported fundraising snapshot. The folder is invented; it does not price the supplies.
BLUE AND YELLOW TAPE. Packing tape carries Ukraine’s colours across neighboring cartons: a symbolic connection between solidarity and practical support.
THE PINEAPPLE ENVELOPE. A pineapple stamp and blank sender line recall card 050, The Pineapple Fund. This crossover does not identify an actual donor.

078.alt: FIVE OF NINE GUARDIANS. Five red strings control five central guardians; four blue guardians stand free. This represents the five-of-nine validator threshold, not nine individual people.
THE ETHER RESERVE. Violet Ethereum-shaped crystals and the 173,600 ETH label recall the stolen Ether. The physical treasure is symbolic.
THE USDC RESERVE. Gold dollar-marked coins and 25.5M USDC identify the second stolen asset. The coins stand for digital USDC, not cash or gold.
THE TEMP TAG. The small tag recalls temporary Axie DAO access that remained available after its intended use ended. The string is an invented visual explanation.

082.alt: THE BOTTLED STORM. The green tornado is a visual pun on Tornado Cash. Its glass enclosure symbolizes attempted containment of intangible software, not an object seized by the government.
THE RED WAX SEAL. The official pressing a seal over the cork represents government restriction. This fictional figure and sealing ritual are not a documented event or an identified individual.
THE GOVERNMENT OFFICE. Formal furnishings and the classical building outside evoke Treasury and OFAC. The office is an imagined setting, not a verified reconstruction of where the decision was made.

THE PAPER TRAIL. Sheets on the desk suggest administrative orders and sanctions documentation. They are illustrated props, not authentic records, readable orders or evidence against a particular person.

079.alt: THE FAINT TERRA EMBLEM. The emblem sits within the cratered moon rather than floating above it. It identifies Terra in a fictional celestial metaphor for the ecosystem’s collapse.
THE BREAKING MOON. The fiery fracture and falling fragments evoke LUNA and a stability mechanism coming apart. No actual lunar event or physical destruction is implied.
THE MARINA BAY SKYLINE. Marina Bay Sands and the lotus-shaped ArtScience Museum make Singapore recognisable. They are an imagined setting, not evidence of an incident at those landmarks.
FIVE RUNNING FIGURES. The five fictional people convey fear and lost confidence. Their number is a composition choice, not a count of victims, founders or institutions.

080.alt: THE FROZEN CELSIUS PURSE. The name on the purse identifies Celsius. Ice around its edge makes the withdrawal freeze tangible: the money is close at hand but cannot be reached.
THE HAND AT THE ZIPPER. A small, familiar attempt to open a purse carries the story. The fictional woman represents frustration, not a particular depositor or a documented event.
THE MANHATTAN SKYLINE. One World Trade Center and the Lower Manhattan skyline place the imagined view across the Hudson from the New Jersey waterfront.
THE IMPOSSIBLE JUNE ICE. Frozen water, railings and snow turn the financial freeze into a landscape. The scene is symbolic, not a historical weather report.

083.alt: The final span. A crane lowers the missing bridge section between two established structures. This fictional construction scene symbolises the integration of Mainnet execution and Beacon Chain consensus.
The Beacon lighthouse. The purple beacon recalls card 062, Beacon Chain. Its guiding light connects the consensus chain launched in 2020 with the network transition completed in 2022.

Builders across the collection. The workers and construction imagery echo card 028, The Ether Sale, and card 032, Ethereum Goes Live. They turn separate milestones into one continuing story of building Ethereum.

A city already alive. The Ethereum emblem hangs over a brightly lit city. Buildings, lights and flowing water suggest an existing world continuing through the transition, not a network being created from nothing.

084.alt: The fallen name. The enormous FTX sign lies on the lobby floor. Its collapse turns the loss of confidence in a familiar brand into a physical image. This is symbolism, not a documented accident.
Trust shattered. The broken lower-right arm of the X exposes its internal supports, with detached pieces scattered nearby. The damaged letter reinforces the editorial caption: TRUST SHATTERED.

A date among dark screens. The desk display reads 11 NOV 2022, anchoring the scene to the Chapter 11 filings. Blank screens suggest interrupted access and uncertainty, not a literal reconstruction of an FTX office.

An anonymous figure. A lone figure stands by the glass holding a sheet of paper. The person is fictional and unidentified, evoking customers and creditors left facing a long process rather than depicting a named individual.

085.alt: The skull mural. The large skull is an artistic reinterpretation of the image associated with inscription 0, not an exact reproduction of that original PNG. Its rough white backing keeps the idea rooted in a physical street-art metaphor.
The zero. The small #0 points to inscription 0. Its recorded December 2022 timestamp is earlier than the 20 January 2023 public announcement commemorated by the card.
A familiar punk. The red-haired character returns from card 038 as an intentional collection crossover. She is not a historical witness or a depiction of the inscription creator.
The second artist. A second figure works beside the mural, turning digital collecting into a shared creative scene. The figures and rainy alley are fictional editorial symbolism.

086.alt: The Doge keyring. A familiar Shiba Inu charm hangs from the shopper's bag. It is a playful collection crossover, not evidence that Dogecoin was involved in the USDC depeg.

The punk pin. The tiny pixel-style punk on the jacket links back to the collection's digital-art story. It is a designed accessory within a fictional scene, not a documented participant or product endorsement.

The HODL cup. A HODL-labelled cup rests on the upper-right shelf in the full artwork. Its message recalls crypto culture's instinct to hold through uncertainty. The tighter card crop partly hides this detail; the full-art book page preserves it.

087.alt: 23 MAR calendar. The desk calendar marks 23 March 2023, when eligible users could begin claiming ARB.
06 FEB snapshot. The screen points to the 6 February snapshot used to establish airdrop eligibility.
ARBITRUM ONE. The network label locates the imagined claim on Arbitrum One, rather than depicting a new network launch.
ETH gas fee. The ETH symbol distinguishes transaction gas from ARB governance tokens. The 0.0012 ETH readout is illustrative.

088.alt: 420.69T supply tag. The tag abbreviates the project's stated 420.69 trillion token supply. It is not a price or market value.
Ethereum hatch. The hatch references the token's Ethereum home. It is visible in the full artwork, beneath the card's lower fade.
RARE PEPES 2016. The binder links back to the earlier Counterparty collectible culture, without equating those assets with the 2023 token.
05 MAY newspaper. The date nods to Binance's 5 May 2023 listing announcement. The newspaper itself is an invented prop.

089.alt: Exchange slips. These symbolic slips reference Ripple's programmatic sales on exchanges, whose circumstances produced a different result from institutional sales.
Institutional sales. The separate red folder recalls the court's finding that Ripple's institutional sales under written contracts were investment-contract transactions.
13 JUL 2023 / 874. The opinion date and tab reference the original ruling, filed as ECF Document 874. The illustrated paperwork is not a facsimile.
NEW YORK LAW / 031. The green book is a thematic link to card 031, BitLicense. Its tab is a collection number, not a docket citation or the legal basis of this ruling.

090.alt: The company binders. DOJ, FinCEN, OFAC and CFTC represent coordinated enforcement with distinct responsibilities. The binders belong to the company side of the story; overlapping settlement amounts should not be added together.

The separate CZ / BSA file. This smaller file keeps Zhao's individual plea apart from the corporate resolution. BSA means Bank Secrecy Act; his plea concerned the failure to maintain an effective anti-money-laundering program.

The empty executive chair. The vacant chair symbolizes Zhao's resignation as CEO. It marks a change in leadership, rather than Binance's disappearance. The chairs and office are invented storytelling details.

The worn BNB folder. BNB / ICO 2017 looks back to BNB's initial coin offering and Binance's beginnings. It connects to card 040, Binance Launches, without suggesting that the ICO itself was the settled offense.

091.alt: The 2013 registration. FORM S-1 / FILED 01 JUL 2013 identifies the Winklevoss trust's early registration statement. This is a filing date, not a denial.
The 2017 disapproval. The upper-left Winklevoss document marks 10 March 2017, when the SEC disapproved the exchange's proposal to list and trade its shares.
The approval at his feet. 10 JAN 2024 points to the single order approving eleven exchange proposals. The paper represents market access, not regulatory endorsement of Bitcoin.
The returning whisky bottle. The bottle on HODL's backpack recalls the whisky bottle in card 021. The returning character links cards 021 and 055 to this moment at the summit.

092.alt: The activation plaque. 269568 above the doorway is the epoch at which Dencun activated on 13 March 2024. The complete number is visible in the full artwork; the card logo partly covers it.
The hourglass tag. 4096 EPOCHS points to the minimum blob-sidecar serving window, about 18 days. It does not mean every copy must be deleted at that exact moment.
A star over Cancun. The star and CANCUN sticker combine Deneb, the star used for the consensus-layer upgrade, with Cancun, the Devcon 3 city used for the execution-layer upgrade.
The cyan data crates. Three luminous crates represent the temporary blob data space introduced by EIP-4844. They are a visual metaphor, not a claim about the number of blobs in every block.

093.alt: The fourth milestone. 840,000 identifies the fourth halving block. NEW SUBSIDY makes clear that the reduced flow represents newly issued bitcoin.
6.25 to 3.125 BTC. The inscription preserves the exact subsidy figures. The smaller outlet contrasts with 015 without shrinking the existing river.
Four tallies. Four engraved strokes above the plaque answer the single stroke on card 015 and mark the fourth milestone.
A familiar explorer. The standing miner repeats the headlamp, teal jacket and backpack from the earlier scene, tying the two cards together.

094.alt: The 2024 envelope. The cream envelope in the satchel answers the future-dated envelope on card 024. Its large 2024 marks the repayment year, not a claim that every case ended then.

Two assets and a route. Tiny asset markings and a boxed routing stamp on the envelope refer to Bitcoin, Bitcoin Cash and repayment through designated exchanges. These miniature clues need the enlarged artwork.
The old withdrawal paper. The worn sheet beside the envelope still reads WITHDRAWAL. It keeps the original problem beside the new correspondence, linking this scene to the customer's earlier wait.
The same locked building. The familiar sign, doorway and chained handles return in sunlight. The setting links the pair; the unchanged lock makes clear that the exchange has not reopened.

095.alt: Two more digits. The $100,000 sign answers the $1,000 marker on card 018. Its 05 DEC 2024 date fixes the later milestone.
The same bull, grown. The chestnut coat, white forehead blaze and single white foreleg carry the young bull's identity into the larger, stronger lead animal.
The following herd. The open space behind the young bull has filled with charging animals. Their varied coats and horns give the crowd its own character.
The familiar way through. The spreading tree, mountain ridge and wooden gate return from Four Figures. Dust and flying earth replace the stillness of the earlier scene.

096.alt: The Solana fairground. Two black Solana flags and the illuminated wheel recall card 056. The fairground once being prepared for visitors now has a new attraction.
The returning professor. White hair, brass goggles and a pale coat identify the professor from 047 and 063. Here he joins the queue rather than working at a desk or experiment.
The copper-haired punk. The orange hair and dark jacket bring back the original character from card 038, carrying the CryptoPunks story into the crowd.
Three days apart. 17 JAN 2025 sits beneath the main marquee. The smaller INAUGURATION / 20 JAN 2025 notice places the launch just before Trump's return to office.

097.alt: The Tucson entrance. The blue canopy, tan facade and prison name identify USP Tucson, where Ulbricht was held. Desert planting places the building in its Arizona setting.
The red-shirt connection. The shirt recalls Ross in 016, Silk Road Shutdown. The older face carries the years between the arrest-era scene and the pardon.
The folded paper. A plain folded letter stands for the act of clemency. Its reverse faces us, leaving the warrant's words to the caption above.
One step beyond. A backpack sits over one shoulder as Ross moves towards the foreground. The entrance recedes behind him, making release the direction of the composition.

098.alt: The face in the glass. The plausible courier becomes a darker figure in the reflection. That mismatch echoes the gap between the transfer shown to signers and the transaction they actually authorised.
Three green checks. Three green checks echo the three signers involved in the transaction. Each light appears reassuring, even though all three approvals belonged to the same deceptive process.
The Ethereum case. The purple diamond marks the assets leaving the Ethereum wallet. Its reflected counterpart follows the same cargo into the scene's darker version.
The cleared doorway. A guard remains at his desk beside the open entrance. The badge and approval lights make the courier's exit look routine; the BYBIT sign fixes the date at 21 FEB 2025.

099.alt: Uncle Sam's grip. The star-banded hat and striped trousers identify the national personification. His hand rests firmly on the Bitcoin, turning the reserve's holding policy into a simple gesture.
The Treasury steps. The columned facade recalls the real Treasury building. The setting points to the department charged with administering the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve.

Hamilton keeps watch. The statue evokes Alexander Hamilton, the first Treasury Secretary. His real monument stands on the building's south plaza, linking an older financial institution to the new reserve.
Not for sale. The plaque condenses the order's rule for Bitcoin deposited in the reserve. Its 06 MAR 2025 date marks the signing, five days before publication in the Federal Register.

058.alt: THE EMPTY THRONE. The blue-and-gold seat remains unoccupied, turning the absence of a reserved founder allocation into the scene's central symbol.
FOUR PROPOSALS. Each participant has a parchment marked PROPOSAL, turned towards its reader. The repeated heading makes debate, rather than coronation, the action.
RETURNING FACES. The silver-haired archivist from 030 returns at the rear left, opposite the copper-haired punk from 038. Their familiar profiles link this council to earlier chapters.
BELONGINGS ON THE TABLE. A closed REALCOIN ledger recalls 030. Across its cover lies the punk's CLAIM / 0 ETH + GAS receipt from 038, bringing two earlier stories into the foreground.

081.alt: THREE ARROWS DOWN. The glowing wall sign turns the fund's name into a direction of travel. The same three arrows reappear on the apron and fries carton.
THE JACKET AND TIE. Office clothes hang behind the counter, close enough to suggest a trading desk has only recently given way to this new shift.
THE RED CHART. On the left, a laptop remains open behind the counter. Its descending red line brings the market's bad news into the warm restaurant interior.
THE NEW UNIFORM. A paper cap and dark apron complete the role reversal. The burger, fries and tray give the caption its literal punchline.

100.alt: THE SHERIFF'S STAR. A plain gold star catches the sunset against the navy coat. The new sheriff gives regulatory oversight a familiar frontier face.
THE NOTICE ON THE WALL. GENIUS ACT, PAYMENT STABLECOINS and 18 JUL 2025 keep the event, statutory subject and signing date visible together.
THE OLDER WANTED POSTER. The Cryptoqueen from 044 reappears on the WANTED poster behind the new notice. This collection callback brings an earlier unresolved story onto the final card's wall.
THE OPEN FRONTIER. The timber porch opens onto a street that continues towards the distant hills, leaving the frontier visible beyond the sheriff and the new notice.
